THE insta-refire teeth. `_check_trigger_radius` (wi_game.gd) runs ONLY from `move_player` -- `load_slot`'s restore never calls it (the doc comment's own guarantee: 'a QA teleport step or a load-slot restore can never ambush the player') -- so the reload landing squarely back inside goblin_encounter_1's trigger_radius must NOT itself spring a second fight. assert_event_count (whole-run, not cursor-scoped) is the precise proof: exactly 1 combat_started so far -- a SECOND would mean the reload alone re-triggered the ambush.

The pre-combat snapshot's player_cell: move_player sets player_cell to the target BEFORE _check_trigger_radius runs, so goblin_encounter_1's own combat_started fired with the player already standing at (30,21) -- Chebyshev 2 from (30,23), exactly the trigger boundary -- and that is exactly where the reload restores them: structurally inside the radius, proven harmless above.

== GH#374, HALF ONE: THE GRACE HOLDS, AND IT IS INVISIBLE ==. The leg above proves the RELOAD itself cannot re-fire the ambush (_check_trigger_radius runs only from move_player). It never proved the thing the playtest actually hit: the player is parked at (30,21), Chebyshev 2 from goblin_encounter_1 at (30,23), so the very NEXT STEP -- any step, in any direction that stays within radius 2 -- used to spring the fight they just lost, forever. The defeat load now arms {until_exit:true, map:floodplains} on that encounter id (combat_screen._close_banner captures Game.sim.pending_encounter() before resolve_combat clears it; game.gd's load_slot arms it on the freshly-loaded sim). It shares warded_encounters with the hearthward charm and is deliberately INVISIBLE: no `cell` key, and world.gd's marker loop skips `until_exit` outright, so the ward render count stays 0 -- a charm the player never cast must never be drawn.

REVIEWER LENS B: the wait above does NOT pin invisibility on its own and must not be read as doing so. `wait_for_event` scans FORWARD from the cursor for the first match, and this map re-renders its wards on every field rebuild and phase crossing -- so a run that drew a charm for the grace (count:1) would simply skip ahead to some later count:0 render and stay green. Verified by mutation: deleting world.gd's `until_exit` skip left this script passing. This is the assertion that actually holds the line -- `assert_event_absent` runs `_has_event`, which scans the WHOLE log from index 0, and defeat_reload never casts a real charm anywhere (the whole-dict `warded_encounters == {}` below is that proof), so ANY count:1 in this run can only be a grace that got drawn. Today the grace is doubly guarded (the marker loop's explicit `until_exit` skip AND the `raw_cell.size() != 2` guard under it); the regression this catches is a future suppression shape that gains a `cell` key and loses the skip.

THE CAN-FAIL, positive half: a REAL move_player DEEPER into the radius -- (30,22) is Chebyshev 1, well inside -- and combat_started must still stand at 1. Without the grace this step is a second ambush; assert_event_count is whole-run, so a re-fire shows up here as 2.
Back to the boundary cell (30,21), Chebyshev 2 -- still inside, still suppressed, and the grace entry is still on the sim.

THE EXIT. (30,20) is Chebyshev 3 -- outside radius 2 -- and _check_trigger_radius erases the grace at its own dist>radius short-circuit. warded_encounters goes empty by WHOLE-DICT compare (blink_bypass_loop's idiom), which is also the proof no real charm was ever created here.

Walk back to (7,6) -- the reverse of the corridor above -- so the ORIGINAL script below (Meet Relc, then the interact-triggered chieftains_raid leg) resumes from its own proven starting cell, byte-unchanged. 14 rather than 15: the grace legs above already spent one net step northward, from (30,21) to (30,20).

== GH#374, HALF TWO: RE-ENTRY RE-FIRES ==. The grace is a reprieve, not a clear -- an encounter you walk away from and come back to must fight you again, or the defeat fix would quietly delete content. chieftains_raid carries its own grace from the defeat above (an interact-only encounter, so the entry is INERT for it -- `interact` routes straight to start_combat, which never reads warded_encounters -- and it is cleared at the first sleep like any other). Route: x=30 is clear floor from y=6 to y=22 (no blocked cells, no wall segments, no other entity) and no other radius-carrying encounter comes within 7 cells of it, so this is a pure approach.
(30,20) is Chebyshev 3 from goblin_encounter_1 -- one cell short of its radius, so nothing has fired yet.

One step back INTO the radius, at the same boundary cell the grace suppressed earlier in this run -- and this time it springs, because the exit consumed the grace and no sleep, charm or dormancy stands in its way.

Play the re-fired ambush out rather than ending the run mid-board: the run's LAST act should leave the harness in a clean, resolved state. The outcome is deliberately unasserted -- this leg's subject is that the encounter is armed again, not who wins it.
